interface.signature: def articulationPoints(V: int, adj: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]: ...

preconditions.expression: V >= 1 and isinstance(V, int) and all(isinstance(neighbors, list) for neighbors in adj) and len(adj) == V and all(len(neighbors) >= 0 for neighbors in adj)
preconditions.description: V is a positive integer representing the number of vertices, and adj is a list of V adjacency lists where each adjacency list contains the neighbors of the corresponding vertex (may include loops).

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(neighbor, int) and 0 <= neighbor < V for neighbors in adj for neighbor in neighbors)
preconditions.description: Every neighbor in adj is a valid vertex index (0 ≤ neighbor < V).

preconditions.expression: all(neighbor in neighbors or neighbor == i for i, neighbors in enumerate(adj) for neighbor in neighbors)
preconditions.description: The adjacency list includes all edges (undirected), and loops (i == neighbor) are allowed.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(return_value, list) and all(isinstance(v, int) for v in return_value) and (return_value == [-1] or all(0 <= v < V for v in return_value))
postconditions.description: The return value is a list of integers where each integer is either -1 (if no articulation points exist) or a valid vertex index (0 ≤ v < V).

postconditions.expression: return_value == [-1] or all(v in return_value for v in set(return_value))
postconditions.description: The return value contains no duplicate vertices if it is not [-1].
The return value is sorted in ascending order if it is not [-1].

postconditions.expression: return_value == [-1] or all(0 <= v < V for v in return_value) and all(articulation_point(v, V, adj) for v in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every vertex in the return value is an articulation point, meaning its removal disconnects the graph into two or more components. The helper `articulation_point(v, V, adj)` is defined as: the graph becomes disconnected when vertex v is removed (i.e., the remaining graph has at least two connected components).

postconditions.expression: return_value == [-1] or all(not articulation_point(v, V, adj) for v in range(V) if v not in return_value)
postconditions.description: No vertex outside the return value is an articulation point (if return_value is not [-1]).
